title: Arranging Coins
summary: Given the integer n, determine how many complete rows of a staircase can be formed with exactly i coins per row, where the last row may be incomplete.
statement: Given the integer n, determine how many complete rows of a staircase can be formed with exactly i coins per row, where the last row may be incomplete.
constraints: Row k needs k coins; return the number of fully completed rows.
reference_solution:
def complete_coin_rows(n):
 left,right=0,n
 while left<=right:
  middle=(left+right)//2
  if middle*(middle+1)//2<=n:left=middle+1
  else:right=middle-1
 return right
hints: Completing k rows costs the triangular number k(k+1)/2.
Binary-search the greatest k whose triangular cost is at most n.
Move right after feasible midpoints and left after infeasible ones; return the last feasible bound.
The triangular cost is strictly increasing, so feasibility is a monotone predicate.
